newsitem.title: CHINA: Hong Kong courts confused over what to call judges.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong courts confused over what to call judges.

text.p: Courts are in a quandary over what to call judges now that Hong Kong has joined China where everybody till recently was called comrade.
Hong Kong's handover to China this week has caused confused legal experts and changed the names of many institutions.
Neither the British-style robed and bewigged judges nor lawyers know what to call themselves, or anyone else, the South China Morning Post said on Friday.
Lawyers asked Justice Frank Stock in court during a murder hearing on the first working day under Chinese rule on Thursday whether he should be called "Your Lordship", as in the former British era.
He said he had no idea and would have to check the handover law to clarify the matter. He was not the only confused party.
Others were so unsure of their titles that they were even consulting the press for advice, the paper said.
A prominent "Queen's Counsel", a British term for senior criminal lawyers, asked a reporter: "What do I call myself now? Am I still a QC or am I something different?"
The newspaper said top advocates would now be known as Senior Counsel.
